name: e85
source: Derived, not independently sourced: an 85% v/v anhydrous-ethanol / 15% v/v gasoline blend (v = 0.85), computed from this project's own data/fuels/gasoline.json (LHV 44.0 MJ/kg, AFR_s 14.5, density 747.5 kg/m^3) and data/fuels/ethanol.json (LHV 26.8 MJ/kg, AFR_s 9.0, density 794.0 kg/m^3; LHV and AFR_s of both from Heywood 1988 Table 9.7; gasoline density = EN 228:2012 range midpoint, ethanol density from Table 9.7's specific gravity - two different sources and reference bases) via ideal volume-additive mixing: rho = v*rho_e + (1-v)*rho_g = 787.025 kg/m^3; mass fraction w_e = v*rho_e/rho = 0.857533; LHV = w_e*LHV_e + (1-w_e)*LHV_g = 29,250,430 J/kg (mass-additive, heat of mixing neglected); AFR_s = w_e*AFR_e + (1-w_e)*AFR_g = 9.783568 (exact in w_e: stoichiometric air per kg of fuel is mass-additive because elemental composition is; w_e itself inherits the ideal-mixing assumption). Assumptions: ideal mixing (any excess volume of mixing is neglected; not quantified here), anhydrous fuel-grade ethanol (EN 15376 blending component), not hydrous ethanol, and a nominal 85% v/v label composition (EN 15293:2018's scope defines E85 as nominally 85 % (V/V) ethanol, also allowing seasonal grades containing more than 50 % (V/V) ethanol, so a real pump E85 may contain considerably less than this file's 85 %.). Range cross-check: 787.025 kg/m^3 is inside EN 15293:2018's 755-800 kg/m^3 density range for E85 at 15 degC.

knock.source: [C] Australian Government, Fuel Quality Standards (Ethanol E85) Determination 2019 (F2019L01265, legislation.gov.au), Schedule 1: minimum RON 100 / MON 87 for E85 of 70-85 % v/v ethanol - interim minimum targets (no RON/MON test method for E85 was available yet) set so that engines can be calibrated to them. Chosen 2026-10-19 (owner decision, vault PHYS-079) as the only cited RON/MON for a blend inside the EN 15293 (50-85 % v/v) and ASTM D5798 (51-83 % v/v) ranges, and as a standard MINIMUM grade like e5/e10. Alternatives (not used): J. Szybist (ORNL), DOE DEER 2012 slides 9-10, measured RON 105.0 / MON 88.7 (ASTM D2699/D2700) [C] on an 'E85' splash blend whose ethanol content is printed as 89.33 % v/v - outside both standards' ranges; EN 15293 minimum RON 104.0 / MON 88.0 (recalled, the previous [AS] value - no copy of the standard available; a web summary of Shell Sweden's E85 sheet gives 104/88 typical and 95/85 minimum, third-hand, not opened); the molar-linear blend rule of docs/data_formats/fuel.md gives RON 107.63 / MON 89.37 [D] for v = 0.85. NOTE: ethanol's charge cooling (latent heat) is not modelled by the knock map, which understates E85's real knock benefit.
